item.title: STAFF POST OPEN- Crosslink Proposal
item.content:encoded:
The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team.

Show Reasoning
– hide block

Crosslink is being proposed due to the connection of glass transfiguration.

Editing this:

In addition, the distorting mirrors found in the “Hall of Fun” are sometimes capable of producing permanent distortions in the people viewing them.

To this:

In addition, the distorting mirrors found in the “Hall of Fun” are sometimes capable of producing permanent distortions in the people viewing them.1

Footnotes
1. Similar to SCP-1225, many of these distortions result in the degradation of the object/subject.

Straight up hate these expungements. Zero context for them, zero purpose to them, zero change in the article if they're removed - so they should be.

Otherwise, as Abettik notes, it's a pretty cool core, and would benefit from some expanded test logs, especially if there's a subtle-but-present theme, or consistency, to the effects. Something to tie it together to give it a little extra punch.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: To expand on my thoughts, I guess that I think the concept is fine: a haunted funhouse/house of mirrors is always cool. However, there's no real cohesion, no underlying theme, nothing to guess at. The SCP is just a standard haunted funhouse. It seems to be randomly screwing with people who enter in completely random ways. The SCP doesn't seem to have any goals or motives, just random spooky stuff. I think you need it to have some difficult-to-ascertain motive that we can partially guess at. Maybe someone was murdered/molested/[REDACTED] by some cult there and they want everyone to know. Maybe its inhabited by an inter dimensional mirror alien or a psycho cult clown. (I thought you were going somewhere with the clown, but he only appeared once.)

I would expect that she freaked out, a crowd gathered, and someone called the police…who said "WTF?" and filed a report. Or perhaps being shrunk was not good for her health, just like being stretched out was bad for the D-class later on. The details of civilian incidents don't always make it into the SCP report…

It's non-canon, of course, but I figure one way the Foundation becomes aware of many SCPs is to spy on police computers and monitor police reports for odd incidents.
